title: Reconciler: one epic at concurrency one — claims, waves, gates, merge, boundary, cleanup ordering, restart from a clone
description: internal/reconcile and ticfac run-epic <id>: read the epic graph through the tk client; claim the next dispatchable tick; start a job through the executor; inspect on a bounded cadence (well under any wipe threshold); collect; boundary-check; merge the attempt branch into the EpicRun integration branch epic/<id>; run the integrated gate from [testing.commands] in .tick/runners.toml (nothing else authorizes shell); close durably through tk only after the gate; clean up only after the close; write a checkpoint on every state change and an attempt record per dispatch through internal/runstate; every effect preceded by the CAS that proves it has not happened. Restart: ticfac run-epic on a fresh clone reads .ticfac/ and adopts live attempts by identity, never redispatches a live one, settles in-flight states from durable evidence, and continues. Appendix A invariants #1-#13 hold; run the lifecycle-invariants suite against the REAL reconciler+executor via an adapter, not only the fake harness. EPIC-SKELETON respected: review and closeout ticks are dispatched last, as jobs (profiles in the next tick). No event bus, no plugin system, no multi-epic.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture epic (3 ticks, 2 waves, review, closeout) completes end to end with a fake runner; restart after dispatch, after collection and before closure produces no duplicate attempt and no false close (three table tests that kill the reconciler at each point and rerun it from a fresh clone); the lifecycle-invariants suite is green against the real components; go test -short ./... green.
